NgraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale: Explanatory context for the generic shape-data exemption removal. Requirements bind only in this bundle's `spec.xml`; this companion adds none. The reviewed approach is variant 1 from `.ngrace/scratch/briefs/GENERIC-SHAPE-DATA-design-review.md`: use the existing explicit file-level marker rather than redesigning the detector. The measured defect is that the pattern detector in `src/review/core.ts` exempts any `src` module whose relative path contains the substring `defect-corpus`, so an ordinary consumer guard named `fixture-defect-corpus-copy.ts`, or any guard under a `defect-corpus-fixtures/` directory, is silently exempted although it holds a production guard. The explicit marker `@ngrace-review-shape-data` (`SHAPE_DATA_MARKER`) already expresses the intended opt-in for a module that holds detector shapes as data, and is the remedy correction 88 chose over a directory prefix. Removing the filename branch restores generic filename behavior while keeping the marker contract, its visible `shapeDataExemptions` reporting, the detector rules, the finding code/severity, and the scan population intact. The internal `src/test-support/defect-corpus.ts` is fixture construction and intentional defect injection, verified from the whole module and real CLI probes, so it carries the marker legitimately; it gains only a comment, not a behavior change.

Alternatives.Alternative: Redesign the detector to distinguish fixture literals from runtime guards without an annotation. Pros: could reduce manual opt-ins and inspect mixed fixture/runtime modules more precisely. Cons: changes source-analysis semantics beyond the confirmed filename privilege and requires its own larger design and generalization controls; it is not required to repair the privilege. Rejected in favor of the existing marker, which gives this small bundle a defined consumer contract.

Keep a narrower filename-based exemption (for example an exact-basename match instead of a substring). Pros: preserves the internal corpus exemption without touching its source. Cons: still lets a consumer filename stand in for the explicit content-based contract, and the defect measured is precisely that inference; it would leave the reviewer blind to a production guard under that name. Rejected.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: Internal-history isolation, the generic archive-policy restoration, and portable skill/resource/template teaching cleanup are separate bundles and are not decided here. The corpus annotation in this slice preserves the existing marker contract rather than adding a broader suppression mechanism.

The marker remains a file-level opt-in, not a line-level one, and does not certify arbitrary annotated runtime guards as data. Any move to line-level granularity is out of scope and would need its own design and generalization controls.

Scenarios.Scenario:
Consumer scan decision, after the change:
```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant F as Consumer source file participant C as ngrace review participant D as Pattern detector C->>F: Read source bytes C->>D: Scan file D->>F: Check explicit shape-data marker alt Marker is present D-->>C: Report file in shapeDataExemptions else Marker is absent D->>D: Run existing structural-guard checks D-->>C: Existing finding or no finding end Note over C,D: Filename gives no exemption ```

Existing function and artifact roles; no new runtime classes are proposed:
```mermaid classDiagram class ReviewEngine class PatternDetector class SourceFile class ShapeDataContract class ReviewReport class InternalDefectCorpus ReviewEngine --> PatternDetector : runReview() PatternDetector --> SourceFile : reads and scans PatternDetector --> ShapeDataContract : SHAPE_DATA_MARKER PatternDetector --> ReviewReport : emits existing results InternalDefectCorpus --> ShapeDataContract : declares data role ```
